data.description:
## Description

What: Migrate the three shell call sites in merge-to-main-pr.sh (lines 437/549/1295) to invoke pr-destructive-action.sh, and rewrite the three SKILL.md sites (debug-everything/SKILL.md:1175, phase-10-merge-verify.md:51, end-session/SKILL.md:242) as negative-directive instruction blocks naming pr-destructive-action.sh as the only permitted path. Why: Existing direct call sites are exactly the cross-session-misclassification hazard this epic eliminates; the doc rewrites align human/agent-facing instructions with the structural enforcement. Scope IN: shell call-site migration; SKILL.md negative-directive rewrites (in addition to, not instead of, the hook). Scope OUT: the wrapper (draft-4), the hook (draft-5), the CI scan (draft-6).


## Done Definitions

- The three merge-to-main-pr.sh call sites (previously direct gh pr close/merge/edit/comment at lines 437/549/1295) invoke pr-destructive-action.sh, and the CI scan (sc-5) passes against the migrated tree ← Validates Closure Check: "All call sites in shell scripts that previously called gh pr (close|merge|edit|comment) directly — merge-to-main-pr.sh:437/549/1295 — are migrated to invoke pr-destructive-action.sh. SKILL.md sites — debug-everything/SKILL.md:1175, phase-10-merge-verify.md:51, end-session/SKILL.md:242 — are rewritten as negative-directive instruction blocks naming pr-destructive-action.sh as the only permitted path; the rewrite is in addition to the PreToolUse hook (which is the load-bearing enforcement)."
- The three SKILL.md sites are rewritten as negative-directive blocks that name pr-destructive-action.sh as the only permitted path and prohibit direct gh pr destructive invocation ← Validates Closure Check: "All call sites in shell scripts that previously called gh pr (close|merge|edit|comment) directly — merge-to-main-pr.sh:437/549/1295 — are migrated to invoke pr-destructive-action.sh. SKILL.md sites — debug-everything/SKILL.md:1175, phase-10-merge-verify.md:51, end-session/SKILL.md:242 — are rewritten as negative-directive instruction blocks naming pr-destructive-action.sh as the only permitted path; the rewrite is in addition to the PreToolUse hook (which is the load-bearing enforcement)."
- merge-to-main-pr.sh's existing behavior (PR close/merge on the session's own PR) still passes its end-to-end test after migration, proving the wrapper substitution is behavior-preserving for the owning session ← Satisfies: sc-3

## Considerations

- [Ordering] Depends on draft-4 (wrapper) and draft-6 (CI scan) existing; migrating before the wrapper exists would break the call sites.
- [Negative-directive] Per the R2 lesson, SKILL.md rewrites must be prohibitions pointing to the single permitted path, NOT procedural 'remember to invoke X before Y' composition.
- [Line-drift] The cited line numbers (437/549/1295, 1175/51/242) are point-in-time; migrate by matching the destructive call pattern, not by trusting absolute line numbers.
- [Ordering/self-block] draft-5 (hook) and draft-6 (scan) enforce the single-permitted-path invariant; until this migration lands, merge-to-main-pr.sh still calls gh pr directly. Confirm the PreToolUse hook (draft-5) inspects ONLY the top-level Bash tool command string (e.g. 'merge-to-main-pr.sh ...') and NOT the script's internal gh pr subprocess calls before relying on it — otherwise the hook would brick the merge pipeline. Migrate the merge-to-main-pr.sh call sites in the SAME change that the hook/scan would otherwise reject, so the pipeline is never blocked mid-epic.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a DSO maintainer, I want all existing direct gh pr destructive call sites migrated to the wrapper and the SKILL.md prose sites rewritten as negative directives
